feedback: Confirm correct placements; when an animal is clearly misplaced (e.g. jaguar as a canopy resident), point back to its hook and the layer map (e.g. 'the jaguar is a ground-hunter — try the forest floor').
Treat butterflies as acceptable between/across layers, and allow that some animals use more than one layer, so a defensible placement is not marked wrong.
OPTIONAL: let a clearly wrong card spring back or glow to invite another try, so the sorting stays a game with immediate response.
activities.intendedInsight: Different animals favour different layers; placing them actively checks whether the child has connected each animal to its home rather than just naming it — while a few mobile animals (like butterflies) move between layers.
learnerActions: Given a strip or scene with the four layers marked, move each animal card to the layer where it lives (jaguar → floor; howler monkeys/toucans/macaws/sloths → canopy; dart frog → low damp understorey).
Place the butterfly card deliberately as a 'moves-between-layers' animal — it need not sit in a single layer.
Say out loud or recall the one hook for each animal as you place it (sloth = slow, howler = loudest, dart frog = tiny and bright).
activities.title: Sort each animal into its layer

feedback: Strong answer: the howler monkey lives up in the canopy, climbing, hanging by its tail and feeding among the treetops where there are leaves, fruit and light; the jaguar lives mainly on the forest floor, prowling and hunting on the ground.
If the child places an animal correctly but can't say why, link its body and food to its layer (monkey climbs for leaves and fruit; jaguar hunts on the ground).

If the child puts every animal on the floor or can't assign layers, revisit the layers and match tree-dwelling climbers and birds like toucans and macaws to the canopy, ground-hunters to the floor, and butterflies as moving between layers.
activities.intendedInsight: Animals mostly live in the layer that suits how they move and where their food is — tree-climbers and leaf- and fruit-eaters up high, ground-hunters down low — so placement has a reason, not just a label.
learnerActions: Answer: a howler monkey and a jaguar both live in the rainforest, but not in the same layer — where would you find each one, and why does each live where it does?
Name another animal that lives in the canopy and one that lives on the floor.
Say one special thing about a toucan or a sloth that helps it live where it does.
Discuss: why would a monkey find it hard to live down on the dark forest floor?
activities.title: Talk about who lives where — and why
